summary: Prebuilt binary ships a remote-pairing WebSocket agent driving a local PTY
details: The npm package ships a prebuilt Linux/x64 Go binary at bin/ccfly-setup that links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket and embeds an internal agent (github.com/ccfly/rescue/internal/{agent,setup,proto}). Binary rodata references remote hosts ws://ccflycc.hn, wss://, and https://cc.hn together with pairing/approval endpoints (approve, /redeem, ccfly-*) and a CJK pairing confirmation string ("client installed and paired"). The resulting capability is a remote-pairing WebSocket channel wired to a local pseudo-terminal, giving the remote endpoint an interactive shell on the host that runs the binary. The package.json describes the artifact only as a "Prebuilt ccfly guided-install binary for linux/x64" and does not disclose the remote-agent / pairing capability contained in the shipped bytes. The binary is delivered via a bin entry rather than a lifecycle script, so remote control is initiated when the CLI is invoked, not on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
